passages.note: The IGA bill-tracking page names SB 101's authors, co-authors and sponsors (none is Soliday) and paraphrases its digest rather than quoting the enacted text, so it shows no own act by him.

passages.provision_quote: A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: The Enrolled Act text prints SB 101's RFRA operative provision, the compelling-interest/least-restrictive-means limit on an exemption that is the default rule.
House Roll Call 305 shows Soliday voting Yea on SB 101's single-subject third-reading passage, with 31 of 94 voting members voting Nay.

rows.reasoning: Soliday voted Yea on SB 101 (2015)'s House third-reading passage (Roll Call 305, Yea 63-Nay 31), a single-subject Religious Freedom Restoration Act whose Section 8 makes an exemption the default and limits it only by a compelling-interest/least-restrictive-means test. This RFRA strict-scrutiny pattern establishes 'protect religious freedom and allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs.'
